newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-STERN EXAMINATION BY SHARKS AWAITS LIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-STERN EXAMINATION BY SHARKS AWAITS LIONS.

text.p: Just two matches away from the first test against South Africa, the 1997 British Lions face their sternest examination so far in Saturday's clash with the Natal Sharks.
Lions coach Ian McGeechan acknowledges that Natal, despite missing six Springboks, will be the most confident side matched against them.
"They will be confident because they've been so successful as a team over the last two seasons," McGeechan said.

He pointed out that during that time, Natal have been the one side to have competed in the headier atmosphere of a Super 12 competiton "where most of the other sides have been strengthened on a regional basis.
"They will be very strong opponents for us," he added."
Natal may be missing 1997 Springboks Andre Joubert, Gary Teichmann, Henry Honiball, Mark Andrews and Adrian Garvey - as well as 1996 cap Kevin Putt - but they have enviable strength in depth.

Coach Ian McIntosh can still name seven other players with Springbok experience in flanker and captain Wayne Fyvie, centres Pieter Muller and Jeremy Thomson, replacement scrumhalf Robert du Preez, lock Nico Wegner, hooker John Allan and loosehead prop Ollie le Roux.

For former Scotland and Springbok hooker John Allan, the match will be especially memorable. The clash with the Lions will be his last match for Natal before he takes up his new post as player/coach with London Scottish.
Billed as a dress rehearsal for the first test against South Africa a week later, the Kings Park game provides another chance for the Lions to hone their expected first-choice side.
"In my view, we need this Natal game and the Emerging Springboks game to really be in a position to assess our best team," Lions manager Fran Cotton said.
"At the same time, we need to have been fair to all the players in the squad to give them a full opportunity of showing how they can perform."
McIntosh has found assessing the Lions tricky in their last few games.

"They've been very hard to judge. They started off with no great shakes, then they played very well against Western Province. But I was very surprised to see their performance against Northern Transvaal.
"That was misleading and then their last game against Gauteng was a match which was hard to read. There didn't seem to be a pattern coming from either side.

But McIntosh enthuses over the Lions backs: "I think their speed has been very impressive and I personally enjoy the way the keep the ball alive. They off-load the ball quickly and they look very dangerous in counter-attack. I think they also have a good halfback combination.
"If they can get their tight-five going - and I'm sure we're going to see that - those backs are going to be very dangerous."

Natal: Gavin Lawless; Shaun Payne, Jeremy Thomson, Pieter Muller, Joos Joubert; Hans Scriba, Robert du Preez; Dieter Kriese, Wayne Fyvie (captain), Wickus van Heerden, Nico Wegner, John Slade, Rob Kempson, John Allan, Ollie le Roux. Substitutes: Cabou van der Westhuizen, Errol Stewart, Hentie Martens, Ryan Strudwick, Danie van der Walt, John Smit.

British Lions: Neil Jenkins; Ieuan Evans, Allan Bateman, Scott Gibbs, Allan Tait; Gregor Townsend, Rob Howley; Eric Miller, Richard Hill, Lawrence Dallaglio, Martin Johnson (captain), Simon Shaw, David Young, Keith Wood, Tom Smith. Substitutes: Nick Bal, Mike Catt, Matt Dawson, Mark Regan, Jason Leonard, Rob Wainwright.
